title: Are brain waves the next unlock for physical AI?
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: Forget YouTube videos—frontier physical AI models need multiple camera angles, dense annotation, and soon, brain wave readings.
body:
Encord, in partnership with German neuroscience startup Zander Labs, has launched a pilot project that captures human brain‑wave activity while a trainer manipulates a wooden block tower. The trainer wears an EEG‑enabled headset that records neural signals alongside video of the task, allowing the team to label each frame with inferred mental states such as error, intent, and surprise. This enriched dataset is then fed into robotics models to see whether the added neuro‑cognitive context improves learning and performance in physical AI systems.

The approach tackles a core bottleneck in humanoid and warehouse robotics: the scarcity of high‑fidelity, real‑world training data. By augmenting conventional video‑based data with direct measures of the trainer’s cognitive state, Encord hopes to create a more informative training signal that could reduce the amount of raw data needed to achieve robust robot behavior. Early results will determine if the brain‑wave‑tagged data yields measurable gains before any broader rollout.

For developers and researchers, this experiment offers a new avenue to enrich training pipelines beyond pure perception, potentially accelerating the deployment of adaptable robots in complex environments. If successful, it could spur a wave of neuro‑augmented data‑generation tools, shifting the focus from model architecture alone to the quality and richness of the data fed into those models.
